articles.summary: Porous bioprinted hydrogel stems reduce flexural rigidity by about 38% relative to solid controls. Responsive leaf modules change curvature with temperature and salinity, yielding a modular aquatic soft machine. The architecture may inform distributed responsive materials, but quantitative biomedical sensing is not demonstrated; the preprint is not peer reviewed.
